remaining_work: The `bytes` component of the anchor is fail-CLOSED but can false-positive: a rename PR that also changes the emitted data object's size (e.g. declares a previously-inherited override, lengthening the vtable) reports a loss while verifiedBytes RISES. Verified by construction; the diagnostic is distinguishable (a 'lost 1 exact symbol' line with no accompanying 'verified bytes fell' line). Out of scope for this issue, whose acceptance wording is explicitly same-addr-same-bytes. Worth an issue if a downstream rename PR hits it.

The producer's prose for the mirrored differingSymbols direction ('a genuinely new differing symbol has no departure to answer it') is imprecise: a DIFFERS->VERIFIED fix also produces a departure. The CODE is nonetheless sound -- the property that holds is stronger and was proved separately: a cancellation requires a base differing row at the SAME (module, addr, bytes), so no anchor that was CLEAN on base can newly differ without a report, and the per-anchor differing count can never rise unreported. Comment wording only; no code change needed.

findings.claim: 'A natural `new daMip_c()` would select the global `operator new`, which this image does not contain'
findings.measurement: FALSE. config/arm9/symbols.txt:1633 carries `_Znwj kind:function(arm,size=0xc) addr:0x0203cbe4`, and main carries src/_Znwj.cpp defining it. config/arm9/symbols.txt:1634 likewise carries `_ZdlPv` at 0x0203cbf0. The real, measured barrier is the one src/actors/Scuttlebug.cpp:196 states - 'Natural `new` selects the wrong allocator': the cartridge's factory calls fBase_c::operator new (_ZN7fBase_cnwEj), and mwccarm rejects an in-class operator new (include/fBase_c.h:150, accurately cited), so `new daMip_c()` would link but emit a call to the WRONG callee. The conclusion (keep the literal seam) is right; the stated reason is not, and the handoff's claim that Scuttlebug 'records the same measurement' misstates what Scuttlebug records. The committed source is clean on this point - include/daMip_c.h:153-156 and the src/actors/daMip_c.cpp classInit comment both state it correctly.
findings.note: include/fBase_c.h:155-157's own claim that the global _ZdlPv 'exists nowhere in this image' is contradicted by the same symbol table. Pre-existing on main, not this candidate's, but it is what the handoff leaned on.

findings.claim: Remaining debt is seven padding spans, mState, the daMip_cSelf shadow struct, one V3Blk block and the ov085 file statics.
findings.measurement: Materially understated on the dimension PIPELINE names ('Fields and object layout recovered versus raw-offset or shadow-struct accesses'). Measured in src/actors/daMip_c.cpp at this commit: 15 block-scope shadow-struct declarations across 9 distinct names (Mtx43 x4, Vector3 x3, V3 x2, Vector3_local, VObj, Obj, RG, G, V3Blk) - only daMip_cSelf and V3Blk are named; 63 block-scope extern declarations naming 26 distinct objects, several with contradictory types for the same object (data_ov085_021305c0 appears as int[], struct G, void*[] and char); and 18 `(char *)this` casts bound to c/self/p, driving 187 raw-offset accesses on 165 lines over 39 distinct offsets, 28 of them at or above 0x110. FOURTEEN of those 28 are offsets the header ALREADY names or types: all five typed sub-objects (0x110 mdCcAc_c, 0x144 mWithMeshClsn, 0x300 mModelAnim, 0x368 mShadowModel1, 0x3c0 mShadowModel2) plus 0x426 unk_426, 0x427 mTalkState, 0x429 mIsGlowing, 0x438 mPathId, 0x43c mRabbitId, 0x440 mCharacterId, 0x444 mNumPathNodes, 0x448 mPathNodeIndex and 0x45c mTalkingPlayer. The header's named fields are used ~97 times, so both spellings coexist throughout. Additionally mTalkingPlayer is documented in the header as 'A Player *' but declared s32 - the same debt class as mState, and unlisted.
findings.note: None of this is a byte defect and none of it is unusual for a first promotion. The defect is that the handoff's account of this dimension would lead a reader to the wrong conclusion, and PIPELINE requires the dimension recorded honestly.
